**GOOGLE AI OVERVIEW** (All tab; sources: Academia.edu):

"The Ω erratum — Sappho, Mother of the Logos: The Transmission Chain from Fragment 31 to the Apocalypse, with Longinus as the Key" is a 2026 academic paper written by Lee Sharks and published in Grammata: Journal of Operative Philology.
The paper treats the religious and philosophical concept of the "Logos" (the Word) as a piece of textual engineering. It studies how a spoken voice can survive past death by turning into written text.
Core Arguments of the Paper
Sappho 31 as a Blueprint: The author argues that the ancient Greek poem Sappho 31 is the founding document for this technology. The poem describes a body breaking down channel by channel. It turns the human body into a physical surface ready for writing. [Academia.edu]
The Key Witness: The ancient text Peri Hypsous (On the Sublime) by Longinus acts as the main bridge. It is the only ancient document that connects early Greek love poetry directly with the creation commands in Genesis. [Academia.edu]
Grammar Without a Doer: The paper focuses on unique grammatical structures. These include meaning without voice, commands without a clear executor, and actions without a named doer. This structure forces the reader to complete the text's meaning. [Academia.edu]
Structure of the Evidence
The author organizes the research into three layers:
A Hard Center: This layer looks at the exact transmitted text of the poem, ancient grammar, and historical proof.
An Interpretive Ring: This layer brings in philosophical views from Plato's Phaedrus and Philo's ideas on creation.
An Outer Ring: This layer offers a hypothesis tracking how these textual habits influenced the biblical Book of Revelation (the Apocalypse).
